title: Lesson 5: Severing the Chain of Craving — The Reversal of Dependent Origination

suttaRef.title: The Greater Discourse on the Destruction of Craving (MN 38)
suttaRef.excerptPali: 'Aññatra, bhikkhave, paccayā natthi viññāṇassa sambhavo'ti... Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu channaṃ phassāyatanānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ viditvā anupādā vimutto hoti — ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu taṇhākkhayavimutto.
suttaRef.excerptTranslation: 'Apart from conditions, monks, there is no arising of consciousness'... When a bhikkhu understands as they really are the arising, passing away, gratification, danger, and escape regarding the six bases of contact, he is liberated through non-clinging: this is called a bhikkhu liberated through the destruction of craving.

pariyatti.shortSummary: If the forward mode explains the genesis of suffering, the reversal mode (*Paṭiloma*) unlocks Nibbāna. When Ignorance is supplanted by Wisdom (*Vijjā*), Craving is eradicated; with craving quenched, clinging ceases; with clinging quenched, becoming ceases; the entire mountain of samsaric agony dissolves.

coreConcepts.definition: The cessation dynamic: cessation of condition yields cessation of effect, extinguishing Dukkha.
Total extinguishment of psychic thirst, synonymous with the realization of Nibbāna.
Arising, passing away, gratification, danger, and escape regarding sensory experiences.

pariyatti.expositionMarkdown:
### 1. The Sāti Heresy: Consciousness as Soul
Monk Sāti asserted: 'Consciousness migrates unchanged.' The Buddha sternly rebuked: 'Fire burns dependent on timber; remove timber, fire extinguishes. Consciousness arises strictly dependent on conditions!'

### 2. The Absolute Liberation Equation
Ignorance ceases ➔ Fabrications cease ➔ Craving ceases ➔ Clinging ceases ➔ Birth, aging, death, sorrow, and despair cease forever. This is Nibbāna!

commonMisconceptions.correction: Suicide is driven by intense aversion (*Vibhavataṇhā*), plunging one into wretched realms. Canonical cessation is extinguishing delusion with wisdom.

commonMisconceptions.mistake: Viewing Nibbāna as a physical celestial paradise in the clouds.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Nibbāna is the cool, unconditioned state of consciousness wholly purged of greed, hatred, and delusion here and now.

patipatti.practiceGuide:
1. Contemplate Cessation (*Vaya-dhamma*): When anger or craving cools down, spend 30 seconds relishing its absence—taste the peace of the extinguished flame.
2. Cultivate Dispassion (*Nissaraṇa*): Discern the anxiety inherent in luxury acquisitions.
patipatti.suggestedVirtue: Fearless relinquishment, inclining heart toward the peace of Nibbāna.

pativedha.reflectionPrompt: Do you realize that extinguishing a feverish craving yields peace a thousandfold deeper than gratifying it?
selfAuditChecklist: I savored serene relief upon completely relinquishing an addictive craving.
I dissolved the lingering superstition of an immortal static soul.
My heart yearns for liberating purity above worldly fame and fleeting gain.
